title: Adapter secrets upload
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/adapter/secrets, application/json, with which an adapter stores its secrets in the control plane: the values it needs to reach its source, such as a private key the source issued to it when it was set up there. The adapter uploads them once it is set up at its source, before it sends its start-up body again without setup_url (adapter.schema.json), and again whenever a value changes. Each upload replaces every secret the control plane holds for the adapter. The values travel sealed, never in clear: sealed is adapter-secrets-plaintext.schema.json, sealed with HPKE base mode, the suite x25519-sha256-aes256gcm, to the control plane's server key that server_key names, one the adapter pinned at enrolment. The recipient's X25519 public key is that Ed25519 public key converted to its Montgomery u-coordinate, as accesskey's PublicKey.X25519 converts it. info is qory adapter secrets upload v1, a zero byte, the suite's three ids 0x0020, 0x0001 and 0x0002 as u16 big-endian, and lp(server_key), the key as sealed.server_key writes it; aad is lp(adapter id) and lp(access key id), the adapter id the control plane enrolled the adapter as and the id of the access key that signs the request. lp is a u16 big-endian length, then the bytes. The control plane builds info and aad from server_key, the adapter it enrolled and the access key the request verified under, never from other values of the body, and opens the seal with the private half of the key server_key names. It refuses, 400 invalid_request, an upload sealed to a key it does not hold, one that does not open, a plaintext that breaks adapter-secrets-plaintext.schema.json, and a secret whose name the source role of the adapter's latest description does not list under secrets (description.schema.json). The control plane never logs a value, and never shows one: a person sees the names alone. On success the control plane answers a signed 204 with no body. The adapter reads the values back with GET /v1/adapter/secrets (adapter-secrets-answer.schema.json). It is signed with the adapter's access key as definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401; definitions.schema.json has the replay rule. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.

sealed.description: The secrets, sealed to the control plane's server key.

server_key.description: The server key the values are sealed to, one the adapter pinned at enrolment, as the pin writes its public key.

ct.description: The ciphertext of adapter-secrets-plaintext.schema.json, followed by the 16-byte tag.
